basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 22:13 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 206. Unde aries iste, qui pro Isaac immolatus est (Gen. XXII, 13), venerit, solet'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 206. Unde aries iste, qui pro Isaac immolatus est (Gen. XXII, 13), venerit, solet quaeri: an [de] terra ibi subito creatus esset, vel aliunde ab angelo allatus?-- Resp. Aries iste non putativus [ Ms., putatus], sed verus esse credendus est. Ideo magis a doctoribus aestimatur, aliunde eum angelum attulisse, quam ibi de terra, post sex dierum opera, Dominum procreasse.
